snippet.title: IKEA Sustainability Report FY23 Highlights
snippet.description:
2023 was another challenging year for people and businesses around the world. In difficult times such as these, we believe it’s more important than ever not to lose focus on our sustainability ambitions. We need to work even harder to keep moving in the right direction.

This year, we decreased our climate footprint by 22% in absolute terms compared to baseline FY16. We’ve also updated our climate goals and accelerated our climate actions in line with the 1.5°C trajectory and the SBTi Net-Zero Standard. 

We’ve taken many other actions during the year, including, for the first time, using bio-based glue at an IKEA Industry board factory. As glue represents approximately 5% of the total IKEA climate footprint, moving from fossil-based to bio-based glue is key to reaching our overall climate goal. We’ve also pioneered a new technology that enables fibreboard recyclability.

We’ve reduced the amount of plastic packaging in consumer goods by approximately 47% and decreased the total plastic packaging (including consumer packs, multipacks, unit loads and handling materials) by approximately 44% compared with FY21.

We’ve continued our work contributing to a fair and equal society, including launching our updated People Strategy to strengthen our direction and ambition for equality, diversity, and inclusion.

You can read about our progress in the IKEA Sustainability and Climate Reports FY23.

snippet.title: Five Ways to Reduce Food Waste, with Baguette & Butter
snippet.description: We all create food waste, but with smart thinking and good habits such as storing food correctly, we can save money and live more sustainably at home. This is what sustainable food activist and chef Amanda, of Baguette & Butter, teaches in this informative workshop for the IKEA Virtual Greenhouse. snippet.title: Step-by-step kokedama ball making, with We Smell The Rain
snippet.description: For the IKEA Virtual Greenhouse, We Smell The Rain shows how to make a kokedama ball. Kokedama is a traditional Japanese art form also known as ‘poor man’s bonsai’. It’s a meditative technique for connecting with nature and making your own living art piece, combining soil, moss and thread to create a self-contained plant vessel. As well as listing the simple tools for making a kokedama, the film shows tips like which soil to use kokedama balls, how to water a kokedama ball and kokedama styling.

snippet.description: This Honey Fingers workshop for the IKEA Virtual Greenhouse discusses which four flowers to grow at home to nourish bees. Growing bee-friendly plants is important, not only to help protect the honeybees, but because a wide range of wildlife benefits from pollination. snippet.title: IDAHOT 2020: Be Someone’s Home
snippet.description:
On IDAHOT 17 May, the International Day Against Homophobia, Transphobia & Biphobia, we’re calling on our customers and co-workers to make LGBT+ people feel at home everywhere, every day.

For many of us, a forced quarantine during 2020 has taught us how important our home is. A place where we can feel safe, where we can love and feel loved. But there are some who risk being stigmatised, isolated and discriminated against in their living spaces. For the LGBT+ community, their four walls are not always what make them feel at home and welcomed.

With the Be Someone’s Home campaign 2020, we want to recognise this reality and invite co-workers and customers to be a shelter for those who are discriminated against and struggle to find safety. We can be a safe space for our LGBT+ friends and colleagues, we can be their home.

Everyone should have the right to be themselves. Stand up against discrimination of LGBT+ persons on 17 May, and every day #BeSomeonesHome #IDAHOT

snippet.title: Bridging the imagination gap with IKEA Place
snippet.description:
Everybody is creative, but sometimes we all need a little bit of inspiration to see the real potential in our homes.

IKEA Place lets you try 3D-models of IKEA furniture and room sets directly in your own home. Combining the latest Augmented Reality technology and IKEA smart home furnishings solutions, you can experience IKEA like never before. IKEA Place gives you an accurate impression of size, design and functionality so you can stop wondering and start furnishing. Discover new items and get weekly inspiration to spark new ideas.

Features:
● Browse, search and place your favourite IKEA furnishings
● Save a room to revisit and reiterate later, or co-create with others
● Make a favourite list and buy via a link to IKEA.com or the IKEA Store app
● Receive product news and exciting ideas for life at home
● Weekly inspiration curated for you
● Point your camera at any piece of furniture and discover similar IKEA products using Visual Search.

Let things fall into place.

snippet.description:
IKEA has partnered with social entrepreneurs since 2012. Through the partnership over 20 000 jobs have been created for people who need it the most – vulnerable and marginalised groups who have difficulties getting into the labour market. It is done through business – co-creating products and services available at IKEA stores around the world.  IKEA also does it through backing and boosting social entrepreneurs whose work is not related to producing IKEA products or services, by partnering up IKEA co-workers with social entrepreneurs, sharing our business knowledge and networks with them. 
It's about making a positive social impact on people and society, creating long lasting change.

snippet.title: The IKEA meatball – ‘round since 1985
snippet.description: Meet Severin Sjöstedt, the chef behind the original IKEA meatball recipe. Back in 1985 Severin threw himself into the job of creating the perfect IKEA meatball, a challenge that involved long and passionate discussions with his team and Ingvar Kamprad. “Back then, guests in our restaurants were not served in a smooth and quick way and the quality was not good enough,” explains Severin. “It was a serious problem because as Ingvar Kamprad put it: ‘It’s tough to do business with hungry stomachs’”. It took Severin nearly one year to create the perfect recipe. Today more than a billion IKEA meatballs are sold every year. They’re very IKEA – they’re convenient, they’re Swedish, and they’re for the many.

snippet.title: The veggie hot dog – plant-based goodness
snippet.description:
We have challenged ourselves to develop a delicious veggie 
hot dog for the IKEA Bistro – a plant-based, more sustainable option to our much loved iconic hot dog. Plant-based foods need less resources, less water and less soil to feed just as many, while making a smaller carbon footprint. We think healthy and sustainable food should be delicious and affordable, and we want to make it easier to make better everyday choices. So, when you think about it, a veggie hot dog makes perfect sense.

snippet.title: Restoring rainforest in Borneo
snippet.description: Since 1998 IKEA has funded the Sow A Seed project, with the main objectives to regenerate a degraded rainforest on Borneo and to support research in order for others to follow. So far 2 million seedlings have been planted in 18 500 hectares of land, more than 700 people have been employed and a lot of research has been conducted in the largest project of its kind in the world. But most importantly: the rainforest has come back to life.

snippet.title: Skills, Talents and Aspirations
snippet.description:
When people are forced to leave their homes, they have to leave most things behind. But no matter what they leave behind, they all bring three things with them wherever they go: skills, talents, aspirations.

The IKEA Foundation is supporting the International Rescue Committee (IRC) with a €5 million grant to help improve the lives of both refugees and young Kenyans living in Nairobi’s informal settlements. Together we promote refugees’ self-reliance and financial independence. 
 
Refugees and their new communities can thrive together when refugees are able to develop their skills, embrace their talents and fulfil their aspirations. Because when refugees are able to work, they create businesses and employ others. They have more money to spend in the local economy and need fewer benefits. They experience less frustration and feel more connected to their new community, like Patience, Lispher and Sebineza are.

snippet.title: AR gamers try out IKEA Place on Android
snippet.description:
We went down to a park in London, found players of a popular location-based AR game and asked them to try out IKEA Place, the new AR app from IKEA. 

Subscribe to IKEA here:
https://www.youtube.com/user/IKEA?sub...

More information about IKEA Place:
Built using Android’s new Augmented Reality ARCORE, the app includes 3D and true to scale models of everything from sofas and armchairs, to foot stools and coffee tables. Giving you an accurate impression of the furniture’s size, design and functionality in your home.

So now you can stop wondering and start doing.
Find your happy place
1. Make sure you have upgraded your compatible Android device  
2. Search for ‘IKEA Place’ in the App store and then download / install
3. Tap the app, scan your place and then:

- Browse and search IKEA furnishings
- Place furniture in your room and play with where it sits / fits
- A new Visual Search feature allows you to point your camera at any piece of furniture and find the most similar IKEA product.  
- Capture your creations as still or video, then share with
friends & family
- Save a room to revisit and reiterate later, or co-create with others
- Make a favourite list and buy via a link to IKEA.com or IKEA Store app
- Receive product news and exciting ideas for life at home

All eligible full-time co-workers within a country receive the same amount, regardless of their unit, position or salary.
